Final commitments — three prioritized product bets this year: (1) Modular Health‑Score Builder & backtesting, (2) Guided CSM Workflows (rule‑based NBA nudges, contextual task UI, playbook→CRM orchestration), and (3) Outcome & Renewal Reporting (exec dashboards, scenario planning & ROI attribution) — each chosen as must‑ship to move NRR, churn, WAU and NPS.  
GA windows and scope: Health‑Score Builder — pilot months 0–3, early GA to lighthouse adopters by month 6, full GA by month 9 (score editor, templates, backtesting, tenant permissions); Guided Workflows/Automation — NBA pilot months 7–9, NBA + Playbook Automation GA by month 12 (rule engine runtime, task UI, CRM task orchestration); Renewal Reporting — renewal dashboards early GA by month 6, scenario/ROI tools GA by month 12.  
Year‑end lighthouse outcome targets to judge success: WAU lift +15–25 percentage points for adopting teams, renewal forecast absolute error improvement 10–20% for lighthouse cohorts, share of at‑risk accounts “stabilized” +20–30% (targeting a ~20–25% relative churn reduction in cohorts), and CS‑leader NPS +5–10 points.  
Midyear (month‑6) contingencies pre‑approved if a bet underperforms: (A) health scoring fails → pause NBA rollout, reallocate engineering to score backtesting/permissions and ship manual override + safe‑mode for tenants; (B) NBA/automation underperforms → revert to preview‑only recommendations, expand CRM task surface and human‑triggered playbooks while shifting EMs to rules‑engine hardening; (C) reporting/forecasting underperforms → extend pilots, increase instrumentation/analyst support, and defer marketplace/scale work.  
These are firm commitments: we will protect capacity for these three bets and the contingency moves within the ~87 EM budget, explicitly deferring full ML copilot and large real‑time integrations so Engineering, Sales and CS can harden GA releases and deliver publishable lighthouse proof points.
